items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes seems to be enough to get most of the benefit, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Eating dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to a rise in sugar, with dinners from 8-9 pm linked to a rise about 13.3 mg/dL more than dinners before 6 pm. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference for you.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast is currently averaging 12.1 hours, and it might be worth trying to extend it to see if it makes a difference. In one program, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed some numbers by -0.03 points compared to coaching alone.
